Markets & Custody

Nineteen Cents and a $541 Million Exit

OKX perpetuals priced Anthropic’s $2 trillion Nasdaq debut to within nineteen cents, even as BlackRock’s IBIT suffered a record $541 million outflow and bitcoin slipped below $62,000.

At 11:47 a.m. in New York on Thursday, a perpetual futures contract on OKX printed $111.31 for Anthropic; one minute later, the first trade on Nasdaq cleared at $111.50 [s550]. In an offering that raised $81.3 billion and valued the AI lab at roughly $2 trillion fully diluted, the levered crypto venue found the opening price to within two-tenths of one percent before the regulated exchange’s opening auction even finished [s550]. The stock ran to $114.99, closed at $97.17, and drifted to $92.60 after hours [s550].

On the other side of the ledger, institutional bitcoin claims took a beating. Bitcoin slid under $62,000, down 25 percent in a month [s541], while BlackRock’s IBIT posted $541.1 million in net outflows on November 19 — its worst single day since launching in January 2024 — dragging the broader ETF complex to $582 million in redemptions [s534]. Strategy shares fell for a sixth straight session to $86 [s549] as Michael Saylor told investors the company will let its STRC preferred stock shrink from roughly $8 billion toward $5 billion via buybacks and confirmed bitcoin is on the table as a funding source, with $431.8 million already sold [s538].

The contrast drew sharp commentary across the feed. Anthropic is now valued higher than the entire Bitcoin network. I see a massive mispricing and opportunity. wrote Erin [s41]. Rod noted that Dario Amodei is about to learn about being a public-company chief executive and continuous disclosure obligations [s234]. Meanwhile, VanEck served Gemini termination notices across all three of its crypto ETFs — HODL, ETHV, and VSOL — leaving Coinbase as sole custodian starting February 16, 2027 [s533], and in Washington, House Financial Services Chairman French Hill warned the CLARITY Act is likely dead until 2027 [s546].

Security Desk

Bisq Urges Mandatory Patch for Java4Shell

Three security patches headlined a 46-release wire day, led by Bisq 1.10.12 [s522]. Decentralized flagged that the update fixes Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938), a critical remote code execution flaw in the Java runtime, and urged users to upgrade immediately even if they are not actively trading [s317].

Hardware and banking custody fared no better. Ledger confirmed tampered hardware wallets in Berlin and opened an investigation into two more in Dubai [s542]. Citi quietly added Section H to its online user agreement, making customers liable for third-party AI agent actions including losses from credential leaks and hacks [s536]. Separately, JPMorgan Chase disclosed vendor email breaches affecting its Reserve Visa cardholders, prompting Ken 🎋 to joke about listing only the banks that were not hacked this month [s353, s366].

Dispatches & Infrastructure Protocol · Conferences · Field
Open Source

Grasp CI Delegates Builds Across Nostr

DanConwayDev launched ngit-ci v0.2, letting coordinators delegate Nix workflow jobs to compute providers across multiple machines — including a developer’s own Mac — coordinated over the Grasp CI protocol [s131].

Elsewhere on the stack, Mostro shipped Node v0.20.3 with dual-source price divergence guards and range-order fixes [s12], while nostr.mom split into two strfry shards — a 30-day window and historicals — behind a multiplexer proxy to dodge fragmentation [s79]. Amboss reported that two of its three machine-learning Lightning routing papers are now running in production, allocating over $16 million in liquidity across managed nodes [s333]. And Richard Nakamoto launched JustaHeater.lol, indexing more than 200 bitcoin heaters and miners across 32 stores with noise and payback calculators [s246].

On the Ground

El Zonte, Parkes, and Manchester Open Their Doors

Three grassroots gatherings converged on the weekend calendar. In El Zonte, El Salvador, the Global Bitcoin Circular Economies Summit opened to the public for the first time, drawing merchants, educators, and developers from Africa, Asia, and Latin America [s31, s81]. In Australia, the Bitcoin Bush Bash kicked off at Cooke Park Pavilion in Parkes with no ticket or RSVP required [s157].

In Manchester, Nostrshire and Bitfest went live, with Final preparing a presentation on GrapheneOS, UK privacy affairs, and mobile security [s66, s150, s278]. Meanwhile, Frank Corva reported for Forbes on Paraguayans turning curious about Bitcoin following the collapse of Ueno Bank [s171], just days before Mostro’s appearance at Sovereign Conference #1 in Asunción [s11].

Odds & Ends

A 1-in-39 Solo Block and a Flashlight to Voyager

Dr -ck congratulated solo miner 3Hkn~wVKS for solving the 322nd block at US West solo.ckpool.org with roughly 471 TH/s on a 95 TH/s worker — about a one-in-39 chance in a year [s34].

NASA’s Astronomy Picture of the Day featured a time exposure from the Emirates Astronomical Observatory tracing V-G-R in Morse code by flashlight toward Voyager 1, 26 billion kilometers away [s125]. On the daily ledger, WORD5 #777 tested Hard Mode regulars [s15, s197, s207], SatsOil refused Black Friday discounts ahead of its second olive harvest shipment from Sicily [s167, s214], and Rod summed up the morning chorus: Developers create worlds foremost free speech platform where anyone can say anything. And what do people say? They say GM. [s133]
